$comment: Single source of truth for every directory in this repository that is vendored from an upstream project. scripts/sync_vendor.py reads this file to perform both the initial import and every scheduled refresh, so an import and an update take exactly the same code path. Do not hand-edit vendored directories: change the manifest, then re-run the script. A source maps a list of upstream subtrees into its own vendored root, preserving the relative distance between them so links inside the vendored content keep resolving. kind=skill-collection tracks each child directory individually; kind=support copies a linked-into subtree whole.

sources.name: OpenHeart
sources.author: Ahmad Hassan (B-Ted); copyright notice: OpenHeart Contributors
limitations: This is a deliberately selected, non-routable source reference, not the complete OpenHeart application and not an upstream skill.
Do not execute bundled Rust or Python source snapshots. The authored skill runs only its own scripts and does not require the upstream server or compiler.
A pinned reference does not qualify language coverage, numerical claims, benchmark results or synthetic upstream projections.

This is an immutable commit reference with no automatic refresh cadence. Updates are manual and require an explicit ref, expected_commit and pinned_commit change plus source-fidelity and adversarial review.
sources.notes: The local openheart-analysis SKILL.md, workflow, templates, schema, exporter and tests are separately authored outside this read-only destination. The importer preserves original source, selected example output shapes, author credit and the exact MIT notice. Review and update this immutable pin manually; it does not follow the upstream branch.

sources.name: job-hunt-skills
sources.author: Remotivated
limitations: DOCX and PDF export is not vendored. `scripts/export-documents.mjs` needs a checked-in 1.9 MB Node dependency bundle plus a pinned Typst binary, and this repository has no Node CI to keep either honest. Everything the skills do in Markdown works without it. For ATS-safe DOCX and PDF output, clone the upstream repository and run it there.

`scripts/scaffold-state.mjs` and `scripts/profile-strength.mjs` ARE vendored. Both import only `node:fs`, `node:path` and `node:url`, so they run on any Node 18+ with nothing installed. They are vendored because `get-started` calls the scaffolder its "Preferred" path and `_shared/state-layer.md` says the skills run it; omitting them guaranteed a file-not-found for anyone following the primary instruction.

The skills expect a `my-documents/` state layer in the user's own working directory, described in `skills/_shared/state-layer.md`. That is the user's data and is deliberately not vendored. Run the `get-started` skill to create it.

`skills/_shared/` holds a shared instruction contract rather than a skill, so it carries no SKILL.md and is exempt from the per-skill provenance rule. It is imported and provenance-stamped as a shared support directory.

Upstream's own contributor checks (`check-internal-links.py`, `test_skill_contracts.py`, the export tests) are not vendored. Link integrity of the vendored subset is instead enforced here by `scripts/check_links.py` in CI.
sources.notes: The upstream skills carry 47 links to ../_shared/state-layer.md and further links to ../../guides/ and templates/. Copying only skills/ would leave every one of those links pointing at nothing, so guides/, templates/ and the two dependency-free helper scripts are mapped alongside at the same relative distance and the links resolve unchanged. This is why a manifest source declares a list of paths rather than one subdirectory.

additional_licenses.note: Four Gelasio TrueType fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The import's primary MIT licence does not cover them.

sources.name: i-have-adhd
sources.author: Ayoub Ghriss (@ayghri)
limitations: Only the skill is vendored. Upstream also ships tool-specific integrations this library does not use: Claude, Codex, Cursor and Gemini plugin manifests, an OpenCode command and JS plugin, TypeScript extensions under extensions/, and an eval harness under evals/. None are needed to load the skill, and several would require a Node or TypeScript toolchain this repository does not run.
Upstream keeps the skill under .cursor/skills/, so it vendors to skills/i-have-adhd/i-have-adhd/. The inner directory name is the skill's frontmatter name, which SK004 requires them to match.

sources.name: financeskills
sources.author: Ayotunde Oso (@GAJETOso), KOMVIA
limitations: Only the upstream skills/ tree is imported. No Markdown link from a skill leaves skills/, so commands/, tools/, standards/, foundations/, workflows/, compliance/ and projects/ are not vendored. The 52 slash commands under commands/ are wrappers that call a skill by path and are not vendored; the MCP server and helper tooling under tools/ are plugin runtime, not skill content.

Four prose references point at unvendored trees: standards/foundational/practice-standard-earned-value-management, standards/auditing-assurance, projects/context.md and projects/completed-projects/2019/holdings-of-cryptocurrencies/. An agent following them literally finds nothing here.
projects/context.md is a user workspace file, the same way job-hunt reads my-documents/. It is not vendored content.
The upstream validator (validate_skills.py, validate-skills.sh) is not vendored. scripts/lint_skills.py is the only validator this repository runs.
The upstream LICENSE names KOMVIA as the copyright holder while the README credits Ayotunde Oso (@GAJETOso). Both are recorded rather than choosing one.

limitations: automation/skills-lock/SKILL.md invokes the upstream root scripts (generate-skills-lock.py, validate-skills.js) and foundation/using-gtm-skills/SKILL.md invokes install.sh from the repository root. Neither the scripts nor install.sh is vendored, so those commands cannot run in this layout.

23 Markdown files reference other skills by repository path, such as skills/foundation/using-gtm-skills/SKILL.md. After vendoring the same skill sits at skills/gtm-skills/foundation/using-gtm-skills/SKILL.md, so those paths do not resolve. They appear in reading lists, not as executable steps, and the skills they name are present.
using-gtm-skills documents skills.lock and taxonomy.csv at the upstream repository root. Neither is vendored, and its integrity-check instructions cannot run here.
The upstream repository tooling (scripts/, .claude-plugin/, install.sh, assets/, docs/) is not vendored. scripts/lint_skills.py remains the only validator this repository runs.
Eight skills are excluded because their frontmatter names already exist here; the local skill wins. See exclude_reasons.
Many reference files are duplicated across skills upstream. They are copied as-is rather than deduplicated, because the vendor model copies whole skill directories.

sources.name: rederive
sources.author: Eric Zou
limitations: docs/, assets/ and .claude-plugin/ are not vendored. Static relative-link checks found no links under skills/ to them.
scripts/history.sh shells out to git and scripts/structure.py to python3. Both are standard tooling, not bundled dependencies.
The skill writes .rederive/map.md and .rederive/log.md into the target repository. That is workspace state in the user's repo, not vendored content.
